name: Leadership & Vision
description: On leading people, casting vision, and rising to the moment.
author: Quips Editorial

quotes.content: A leader, he said, is like a shepherd. He stays behind the flock, letting the most nimble go out ahead, whereupon the others follow, not realizing that all along they are being directed from behind.
quotes.source: Long Walk to Freedom (1994)
quotes.notes: Mandela recalls the axiom of the Thembu regent Jongintaba in his autobiography; the quoteDate reflects the book's publication year, not a precise day.

quotes.content: Plans are worthless, but planning is everything.
quotes.source: Remarks at the National Defense Executive Reserve Conference, Washington, D.C. (November 14, 1957)
quotes.notes: Eisenhower framed it as an old Army maxim he had heard, illustrating that the discipline of planning outlasts any single plan.

quotes.content: The price of greatness is responsibility.
quotes.source: Address at Harvard University (September 6, 1943)
quotes.notes: From Churchill's wartime speech receiving an honorary degree at Harvard, urging Anglo-American shared duty.

quotes.content: Leadership and learning are indispensable to each other.
quotes.source: Remarks prepared for delivery at the Trade Mart, Dallas (November 22, 1963)
quotes.notes: From the address Kennedy was to give the day he was assassinated; the text was released though never spoken.

quotes.content: A shared vision is not an idea. It is not even an important idea such as freedom. It is, rather, a force in people's hearts, a force of impressive power.
quotes.source: The Fifth Discipline: The Art and Practice of the Learning Organization (1990)
quotes.notes: Senge's definition of shared vision as a felt commitment rather than a slogan; quoteDate reflects publication year.

quotes.content: The first responsibility of a leader is to define reality. The last is to say thank you. In between, the leader is a servant.
quotes.source: Leadership Is an Art (1989)
quotes.notes: The opening frame of the former Herman Miller chairman's book on leadership as stewardship; quoteDate reflects publication year.

quotes.content: The servant-leader is servant first. It begins with the natural feeling that one wants to serve, to serve first.
quotes.source: The Servant as Leader (1970 essay)
quotes.notes: The founding statement of the servant-leadership movement, from Greenleaf's original essay; quoteDate reflects publication year.

quotes.content: A leader is best when people barely know he exists. When his work is done, his aim fulfilled, they will say: we did it ourselves.
quotes.source: Tao Te Ching, Chapter 17 (c. 4th century BC)
quotes.notes: A widely used English rendering of Chapter 17; exact wording (the attribution axis is sound) varies substantially across translations. Date reflects the traditional composition period of the Tao Te Ching.

quotes.content: Management is doing things right; leadership is doing the right things.
quotes.source: Stephen R. Covey, The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People (1989), p. 101, crediting both Drucker and Warren Bennis
quotes.notes: Attribution axis fails: Drucker's own antithesis set efficiency ('doing things right') against effectiveness ('doing the right things') in 1963 and 1974, Quote Investigator credits the management-versus-leadership form to Warren Bennis, and this exact sentence first appears in Covey, who names both men. See ldr-001 for Drucker's documented wording.

quotes.content: Leadership is the art of getting someone else to do something you want done because he wants to do it.
quotes.source: Attributed to Eisenhower in speeches and interviews
quotes.notes: Long and consistently credited to Eisenhower, matching his views, but the exact original occasion is not firmly documented. Date is a broad estimate spanning Eisenhower's presidency, when the remark is usually placed, not a documented one.

quotes.content: The day soldiers stop bringing you their problems is the day you have stopped leading them.
quotes.source: My American Journey (1995)
quotes.notes: Drawn from Powell's memoir and later leadership talks; wording varies slightly across retellings, so marked attributed.

quotes.content: Leadership is the capacity to translate vision into reality.
quotes.source: Attributed to Warren Bennis, leadership scholar
quotes.notes: Consistently credited to Bennis and true to his body of work, but not tied here to a specific book or page. Date is a broad estimate from Bennis's leadership books beginning with Leaders (1985), not a documented one.

quotes.content: A leader takes people where they want to go. A great leader takes people where they don't necessarily want to go, but ought to be.
quotes.source: Attributed to Rosalynn Carter; quoted in Reader's Digest (2003)
quotes.notes: Source axis is uncertain: credited to Carter in Reader's Digest during her lifetime, with no rival claimant found, but no speech, book or interview of hers containing it has been found. Date is the earliest documented printing, not a documented occasion.

quotes.content: Before you are a leader, success is all about growing yourself. When you become a leader, success is all about growing others.
quotes.source: Winning (HarperBusiness, 2005), p. 61, opening the chapter 'It's Not Just About You'
quotes.notes: Verbatim the opening lines of Welch's leadership chapter in Winning, checked against the Internet Archive's scan of the 2005 HarperBusiness edition.

quotes.content: Leadership is not about being in charge. It is about taking care of those in your charge.
quotes.source: Leaders Eat Last (2014) and related talks
quotes.notes: A signature Sinek theme expressed across his book and talks; exact phrasing varies, so marked attributed.

quotes.content: The best executive is the one who has sense enough to pick good men to do what he wants done, and self-restraint enough to keep from meddling with them while they do it.
quotes.source: Attributed to Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.notes: Long associated with Roosevelt and matching his views on delegation; a firm primary citation is not established here. Date is a broad estimate spanning Roosevelt's presidency, not a documented one.

quotes.content: A leader is one who knows the way, goes the way, and shows the way.
quotes.source: Attributed to John C. Maxwell; the saying predates him
quotes.notes: Attribution axis fails: H. Reginald Buckler wrote 'Surely a leader is one who knows the way, who goes the way, and who shows the way' in The Perfection of Man by Charity (1889), p. 107, and Fr. James Keller's 1960 column quoted it as an existing definition, decades before Maxwell. Date is that of the earliest documented printing, Buckler's.

quotes.content: You manage things; you lead people.
quotes.source: Attributed to Rear Admiral Grace Hopper
quotes.notes: Consistently credited to Hopper, who often distinguished managing things from leading people; exact original wording varies. Date is estimated from the earliest documented appearances of Hopper making this distinction in the early 1980s; it was printed in the OCLC Newsletter in 1987.

quotes.content: The greatest leader is not necessarily the one who does the greatest things. He is the one that gets the people to do the greatest things.
quotes.source: Attributed to Ronald Reagan
quotes.notes: Widely credited to Reagan and echoing a broader leadership adage; a precise original occasion is not documented. Date is a broad estimate spanning Reagan's presidency, not a documented one.

quotes.content: The key to successful leadership today is influence, not authority.
quotes.source: Attributed to Ken Blanchard, management author
quotes.notes: A recurring Blanchard theme across his books and talks; not fixed here to one primary source. Date is a broad estimate from the period of Blanchard's books and talks, not a documented one.

quotes.content: It is amazing what you can accomplish if you do not care who gets the credit.
quotes.source: Attributed to Harry S. Truman
quotes.notes: Popularly credited to Truman, who is said to have kept the sentiment on his desk, though the line predates him and is attributed to several people. Date is estimated from the decade in which this exact wording circulated widely; Truman was first credited only in 1988, and the idea traces to a 19th-century saying.

quotes.content: If you want to build a ship, don't drum up people to collect wood and don't assign them tasks and work, but rather teach them to long for the endless immensity of the sea.
quotes.source: Popularly attributed to Citadelle / The Wisdom of the Sands (1948)
quotes.notes: The wording axis fails: this is a popular paraphrase that does not match any exact passage in Saint-Exupery's text, though the sentiment derives from Citadelle. Date reflects the posthumous publication of Citadelle in 1948, from which the sentiment derives.

quotes.content: Nearly all men can stand adversity, but if you want to test a man's character, give him power.
quotes.source: Attributed to Abraham Lincoln
quotes.notes: The attribution axis fails: no primary Lincoln source exists for this line and it is widely regarded as a misattribution. Date is estimated from the earliest documented appearance, Robert G. Ingersoll's Washington address of 16 January 1883, where he said it about Lincoln; the Lincoln ascription appears only by 1931.

quotes.content: If your actions inspire others to dream more, learn more, do more and become more, you are a leader.
quotes.source: Attributed to John Quincy Adams
quotes.notes: The attribution axis fails: this line has no basis in Adams's writings and is a modern quotation without a documented primary source. The century is a broad estimate for the line's modern circulation, not a documented date.

quotes.content: The function of leadership is to produce more leaders, not more followers.
quotes.source: Attributed to Ralph Nader
quotes.notes: Consistently credited to Nader and in line with his public statements, but not tied here to a specific speech or text. Date is a broad estimate from the period of Nader's public statements on leadership, not a documented one.

quotes.content: As we look ahead into the next century, leaders will be those who empower others.
quotes.source: Attributed to Bill Gates
quotes.notes: Widely credited to Gates and matching his stated views on organizations; a precise original source is not established. Date is a broad estimate from the decade in which Gates was writing and speaking about the coming century, not a documented one.

quotes.content: A genuine leader is not a searcher for consensus but a molder of consensus.
quotes.source: Where Do We Go From Here: Chaos or Community? (1967), ch. 4
quotes.notes: Verified in chapter 4, where the sentence opens 'Ultimately a genuine leader is not a searcher for consensus but a molder of consensus.'

quotes.content: Leaders aren't born, they are made. And they are made just like anything else, through hard work.
quotes.source: Attributed to Vince Lombardi
quotes.notes: Long associated with the Packers coach and true to his philosophy; not tied here to a single verified transcript. Date is a broad estimate spanning Lombardi's years coaching the Green Bay Packers, not a documented one.

quotes.content: Being powerful is like being a lady. If you have to tell people you are, you aren't.
quotes.source: Attributed to Margaret Thatcher
quotes.notes: Famously credited to Thatcher, who repeated it; she presented it as a borrowed line, so the exact origin is uncertain. Date is estimated from the earliest documented appearance, an October 1975 Fairbanks Daily News-Miner item crediting the union leader Jesse Carr; Thatcher repeated it by 1988.

quotes.content: Leadership is hard to define and good leadership even harder. But if you can get people to follow you to the ends of the earth, you are a great leader.
quotes.source: Attributed to Indra Nooyi, former PepsiCo CEO
quotes.notes: Credited to Nooyi from her interviews and talks on leadership; not fixed here to a single primary transcript. Date is a broad estimate spanning Nooyi's years leading PepsiCo, when she gave the interviews it comes from, not a documented one.
